purpose: Consolidated work tracker for the Luzon delivery phase. This is not a species checklist, complete waterbody inventory, release manifest, or claim of biological absence.

limitations: The national registry supplies the pinned region, province, and separately represented independent-city baseline; its lower-level locality rows are out of scope. CALABARZON's working municipality/city name-code denominator is separately recorded in national/reviews/calabarzon-administrative-denominator-reconciliation-20261117.json; it contains no boundary geometry.
MIMAROPA is included in the Luzon delivery phase by project convention; administrative membership, island group, drainage basin, and marine study area remain separate relationships.

baselineReviewedDefinition: Use the completion gates in docs/PHILIPPINES_SPECIES_EXPANSION_PLAN.md section 3. A region is baseline-reviewed only after its complete administrative and source-derived waterbody scope is reconciled, source searches and candidate decisions are accounted for, evidence and reuse checks pass, every waterbody has an explicit coverage result, and counts reconcile.

completionGates.requirement: Account for all current provinces, applicable NCR units, independent cities, and needed lower-level locality crosswalks in the pinned administrative snapshot.
Reconcile source-derived marine, brackish, and inland waters, including rivers, tributaries, streams, natural lakes, reservoirs, wetlands, ponds, and islands where applicable.
Process each agreed source/search or record the access, rights, or evidence gap with attempted alternatives and a follow-up owner.
Give each snapshot candidate an evidence-backed admit, exclude, or hold decision. A hold is triage, not coverage.
Validate taxon identity, locality, date, provenance, item and dataset reuse terms, and citation before public projection.
Show a coverage result per inventoried waterbody; no usable record is a visible gap, never a species-absence claim.
Reconcile raw, normalized, mirrored, admitted, excluded, and held counts and list remaining gaps in each regional manifest.

regions.name: Region IV-A (CALABARZON)

appFacingResearchProjection.scope: Attributed, historical Palico-Lian survey-table assertions with unknown observation date; not a current checklist, abundance estimate, or complete regional baseline.

openWork: Reconcile the selected 164 waterbody leads and new source-derived additions against the 120-municipality/22-city locality denominator, including islands, shared waters, and freshwater, brackish, and marine lanes; this locality denominator is not a waterbody inventory.
Keep source-specific survey assertions distinct from the scope file's waterbody/public-admission counters when reconciling CALABARZON counts.

Keep Manila Bay shared with NCR and Central Luzon under one canonical waterbody identity. The 19 November National Museum crosswalk matched all 524 OBIS rows to GBIF occurrence IDs and four of seven Cavite administrative-text candidates; it adds no capture-site or Cavite-water assignment. Reconcile other sources and localities separately; see national/reviews/manila-bay-national-museum-gbif-obis-crosswalk-20261119.json.
Keep the three historical CAS Santa Cruz River records held from public projection and redistributed packages until the Academy clarifies its no-redistribution terms versus GBIF CC0 metadata.
Keep the Laguna Lakeshore Road Network EIS as a West Bay retrieval lead; its mixed 2014/2020 fish summaries lack a verified adult-fish site/date/voucher crosswalk and item-specific reuse approval.
Use independently reusable, site-resolved sources for other CALABARZON inland waters while Taal CAS redistribution terms and Dryad file access remain unresolved.
Reconcile the wetlands denominator, unnamed river/wetland counts, and modeled stream identities before claiming complete coverage.

After eight 19 November CALABARZON source-backed locality batches, the selected 164-lead scope has 80 city/municipality-linked leads, 80 province-only leads, and 4 without any locality code; represented CALABARZON coverage is 15/22 city codes and 49/120 municipality codes. BMB locality contexts include six San Pablo lakes, Yellow/Tadlac/Caliraya, three Laguna cities, three Rizal municipalities, and the separately reviewed NCR localities around one shared Laguna de Bay identity, Tanza for the Tres Cruzes candidate, Rodriguez for Wawa Dam, Cavinti for the NPC-reported Lumot Lake event locality, and the 14-LGU Taal Lake planning cluster; a working Mojicap/Mohicap alias for the San Pablo City lead is supported by LLDA lists. Retain the Tres Cruzes class/identity hold, Wawa boundaries/access limitations, Lumot reservoir extent/identity caveat, and distinguish the Taal planning cluster and all source-described localities from lake geometry. Keep scopeFrozen=false.

The 17 November exact GBIF name/alias screen returned two 1941 CAS preserved-specimen candidates for waterBody=Bay River; both remain held because locality is “3 km from Laguna de Bay” with 1,743 m uncertainty. Thirteen other exact-field searches returned zero and do not establish absence.

The cross-region PAREX Draft and Revised EIS both list six stations on 7 October 2021, but conflict on fish collection method. Their 13-row matrix and 13-row taxonomic table have four different exact name strings each, and their narrative counts do not match the printed matrix. Keep the Taytay, Rizal FWE 6 locality separate from a named waterbody; see national/reviews/ncr-pasig-parex-eis-version-and-fish-table-reconciliation-20261120.json.

The NFRDI 2014–2015 experimental otter-trawl survey reports a historical top-50 fish-and-invertebrate table grouped by broad Manila Bay sectors including Cavite and Metro Manila. It has no digital haul-coordinate table; the table was not transcribed, and the sectors are not municipality or legal-water boundaries. Keep this shared marine evidence research-only; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2017-manila-bay-trawl-sector-catch-scope-review-20261119.json.

The 2018 NAST Manila Bay fish-landing abstract reports 218 fish-and-invertebrate taxa from 16 landing sites (2012–2015), but gives no site-by-site table or capture-origin records. Its dates and three shared authors overlap the NFRDI 2014–2015 experimental-trawl paper, but the sampling frames differ and a data/program lineage is unconfirmed. Do not add the totals or infer sector-level presence; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2018-nast-manila-bay-landing-trawl-lineage-review-20261119.json.

The NFRDI 2012–2015 ichthyoplankton paper reports 3,008 fish larvae across 34 families; the separate NAST abstract reports 860 larvae across 28 families for 2017. Both describe eight stations and share three authors, but station identity is not crosswalked, and the NFRDI article gives conflicting approximate spacing in its abstract and methods. Keep the windows separate and family-level evidence research-only; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2017-manila-bay-ichthyoplankton-source-screen-20261119.json.

Dryad’s public dataset metadata API now returns HTTP 200 for the 2011 Taal barcode record, but version/file-list API requests timed out and the ordinary SpecimenData.xlsx link returned 403. Dryad documents an API token for file downloads; no authenticated route was used, so the spreadsheet, voucher/locality rows, and photos remain uninspected. Keep searching independent CALABARZON inland sources; see national/reviews/calabarzon-taal-aquilino-dryad-api-access-refresh-20261119.json.

regions.name: National Capital Region (NCR)
openWork: The DLSU Animo Repository exposes a 2005 Chavez thesis record and GBIF exposes the same 2006 article as a Plazi CHECKLIST dataset; their abstracts/metadata repeat the already-reviewed five-site study. The thesis PDF link returned 403 and GBIF's direct page/API were unavailable in this review. Neither is an independent occurrence feed or new specimen dataset; no occurrence count or absence claim is made. See national/reviews/ncr-pasig-chavez-thesis-gbif-checklist-lineage-screen-20261120.json.

Chavez et al. (2006) directly reports Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus from its historical Pasig River site in the City of Manila and says P. pardalis was not collected there in that study. Pasig specimens were hand-caught, but collection dates, site-specific voucher IDs/counts, and coordinates are absent. Retain as historical research evidence only; do not infer present presence or species absence. See national/reviews/ncr-pasig-2006-pterygoplichthys-site-evidence-review-20261120.json.

Public 2024 conference programs add ERDB leads for Pasig River phytoplankton, rotifer, and macroinvertebrate work, but provide titles and presenters only. Their linkage to the DENR-NCR fish assessment is unconfirmed; no public site-by-taxon fish dataset was found in the bounded title/agency search. Do not treat program listings as completed surveys, fish records, or evidence of absence. See national/reviews/ncr-pasig-2024-conference-program-lead-screen-20261120.json.

The 17-unit NCR administrative denominator matches PSA's rendered 16-city and one-municipality tables, and PSA's revision notices support its continuity through Q3 2026; the linked workbook itself remains unparsed. The historical 18-item checkpoint is a mixed set of waterway, shared-water, reservoir, watershed, wetland-park, and habitat contexts, not 18 validated waterbodies. The 2025 DENR-NCR Gawad Taga-Ilog review crosswalks 12 selected nominations to 12 reported city/municipality codes. Follow-ups corroborate the BMB Jamboree Lake name/locality and identify a BMB NAPWC pond alias candidate plus a named OSM polygon. The polygon is community mapped; the official shoreline, BMB-to-OSM crosswalk, and conflicting 3.39 ha versus approximate 4.0 ha area descriptions remain unresolved. No current access or fish claim is established. Continue broader freshwater, brackish, marine, and habitat source searches.

Extend the source-named inventory and bounded occurrence screens across freshwater, brackish, and marine contexts without treating selected program nominations or candidate hits as a complete inventory or validated capture sites.

Keep Pasig-Marikina reaches, tidal/brackish waters, Manila Bay, and Laguna de Bay connections distinct. The 19 November crosswalk found the 65 National Museum rows from the NCR administrative query among the GBIF bounding-box records and none in the 524-row OBIS result; this is feed/query coverage, not a Manila Bay or NCR-water assignment. Reconcile other shared-bay sources with L1 and L3; see national/reviews/manila-bay-national-museum-gbif-obis-crosswalk-20261119.json.

The DENR-NCR report remains a system-scope and narrative lead without fish-by-site rows; the Marikina preprint remains an eight-taxon research crosswalk. La Mesa Reservoir has five historical host-fish candidates from a 1989-1990 parasite study (234 examined across taxa), not an abundance estimate; hold its Therapon date conflict and Arius/Netuma identity concern. Lopez (1992) is identified through a 2001 secondary citation, but the original proceedings and its methods, dates, denominators, and vouchers remain unverified. Continue freshwater, brackish, and marine source searches and reconcile all candidates against the incomplete waterbody scope.

The 2023 Pasig–Marikina fish-microplastics paper has an Archium full-text link, but direct PDF and publisher-page fetches returned 403 in the review environment. This is a retrieval limitation, not proof that all readers lack access. No paper text was obtained; its repository withdrawal-label conflict and taxon-to-river assignment remain unresolved. See national/reviews/ncr-marikina-microplastics-pdf-access-followup-20261120.json.

The 2015 BMB guidebook and 2016 bulletin remain vernacular historical fish leads without traceable fish-survey methods. Five exact-text CoL XR searches returned zero. A bounded GBIF spatial search found one iNaturalist Channa striata observation inside the community-mapped OSM lagoon ring, but its 8 m uncertainty exceeds the approximately 7 m point-to-edge distance; GBIF also flags TAXON_ID_NOT_FOUND and the record has no waterBody/locality. Keep it unassigned and research-only. A secondary blog lists binomials without survey provenance; a peer-reviewed NAPWC microcrustacean study is not fish evidence. Seek a directly verifiable fish survey and review current protected-area access separately.

The 2022 PAREX Revised EIS adds a one-day, six-station fish-survey lead along the Pasig corridor, with FWE 6 labeled Taytay, Rizal. The February Draft and September Revised EIS list the same stations/date but conflict on method (electric fishing versus fishing lines); both table versions have 13 binomial rows, four exact names unique to each table, and a 14-species narrative. The Revised matrix marks 11 binomials at FWE4 although its narrative says 12; the Draft says “EWE4.” No corrected matrix or voucher record was found. A separate locality crosswalk did not resolve the station waterbody. Keep labels, coordinates, and method research-only pending field records, a source-matched locality link, and item-specific reuse review. See national/reviews/ncr-pasig-parex-revised-eis-fish-survey-review-20261119.json and national/reviews/ncr-pasig-parex-eis-version-and-fish-table-reconciliation-20261120.json.

The 2019 Makati Public Rail EIS states that fish sampling at its five Pasig freshwater-ecology stations was unsuccessful; those coordinates are for plankton/benthos context, not fish occurrences. Its separate eight-name reported-fish table mixes one informal observation, two secondary citations, washout context, and unsourced rows. Keep all names research-only and continue NCR freshwater/brackish/marine source searches.

The 2018 New Manila Reclamation EIS and its companion hearing report describe the same three-station Pasig survey and repeat a six-brackishwater-species summary dominated by 'Tilapia'. The hearing-report photos are captioned only with ambiguous common names ('knife fish' and 'janitor fish'); no scientific identities or table rows were recovered. Direct PDF requests returned 403, and no taxa, photos, coordinates, occurrences, or safety claims were added. See national/reviews/ncr-new-manila-reclamation-pasig-hearing-followup-20261119.json.

The cited Orozco & Zafaralla (2012) chapter is explicitly about Estero de San Miguel and Estero de Quiapo; its abstract reports Rasbora maculata and Anabas testudineus among four fish taxa, without species-to-station assignments. A related 2008 DLSU article describes the same two esteros and four taxa, but its full text is unavailable. Do not transfer either estero finding to Pasig River or double-count the apparent research lineage.

The public AABE issue PDF includes an Orozco conference abstract that repeats the same two esteros and four fish labels; its cover says December 2012 while the abstract footer says 2010. It adds no station-by-taxon data or independent survey. See national/reviews/ncr-orozco-aabe23-abstract-lineage-access-review-20261120.json.

A separate 2015 AABE conference abstract by Orozco and Tolentino names Estero de Paco and its tributary Estero de Concordia and reports Gambusia affinis, Rasbora maculata, and Rasbora sp. in both; it gives no collection dates, methods, vouchers, or species-by-station table. Rasbora sp. may overlap the named Rasbora species, and the study is not linked to Orozco/Zafaralla's San Miguel/Quiapo survey lineage. Keep these as historical research-only leads; add no species rows, current-presence, safety, or fishing claims. See national/reviews/ncr-orozco-tolentino-2015-paco-concordia-abstract-review-20261119.json.

DOST-PCIEERD's 2010 report lists an ongoing FEU biodiversity project covering Estero de Paco and Estero de Concordia; the 2011 report lists the Pasig River Stewardship program among completed DOST-GIA projects, and the EMB's NWQSR describes the FEU project's seasonal/temporal biodiversity scope. FEU's 2015 President's Report independently confirms Glorina Orozco's AABE25 presentation in October 2014. These sources do not link the abstract to DOST funding, provide fish tables, or establish a separate survey. No additional species evidence or current claims were added. See national/reviews/ncr-paco-concordia-dost-project-lineage-access-review-20261119.json.

Monopterus albus: Ame and Mayor (2021) state 1905, but Guerrero (2014) gives the species-table year as unknown and the cited Juliano et al. (1989) chapter remains unretrieved. Fowler (1918) is a historical inventory citation, not an introduction date; the 2017 paper's abstract says 1917 while its main text says 1918. NMNH records USNM 135196–135209 strongly corroborate the paper's report of 14 lots reidentified from Monopterus albus to Ophisternon bengalense, but the paper prints no numbers and exact linkage is inferred. These are 1908 market-labeled lots, not capture-water records or an introduction date. USFWS (2025) also summarizes separate later Malaysian aquaculture-introduction accounts. Keep Pasig identity and native/introduced status unresolved; see national/reviews/ncr-monopterus-philippines-historical-source-chain-review-20261120.json and national/reviews/ncr-monopterus-smithsonian-14-lot-crosswalk-20261120.json.

A current-name cross-check confirms the six distinct NMT fish-table binomials are accepted names, but does not validate field identification. The seven-row table repeats Lutjanus argentimaculatus and conflicts with the abstract's six-native/one-invasive count; preserve both original rows and keep all specimen and station assignments research-only.

An official BFAR NCR market report pairs Dendrophysa russelii with Alakaak and includes Navotas in its summary source area; the NFRDI name reference also shows that Alakaak is non-unique. This is market and vernacular-name context, not a river-capture or specimen crosswalk. Keep both NMT Lutjanus rows, the Kabang label, and the species-count conflict unresolved; see national/reviews/ncr-navotas-nmt-vernacular-name-crosscheck-20261119.json.

The directly reviewed PSFS proceedings PDF contains only an aggregate 2018 Marikina abstract: 14 species across five sites, no taxon names or station-by-species table. A 2019 PSFS call invited presenters to submit full papers but does not establish this abstract was published separately. Keep the locality, taxa, and non-native narrative unresolved; seek only a separate manuscript or supplement if authors/PSFS confirm one exists.

The 2011 primary paper confirms BMP001-11 through BMP036-11 and the GenBank db_xref records use BPMP001-11 through BPMP036-11; a bounded public search found no independent museum catalog or supplement to resolve the conflict. The paper names five stations but does not link specimens to them. Keep station, voucher, and taxonomic assignments unresolved; see national/reviews/ncr-marikina-2011-source-prefix-and-public-catalog-search-20261119.json.

A local screen of five rounded GenBank coordinate clusters against geoBoundaries 2020 ADM3 polygons places four inside Marikina and one in Rodriguez; one lies close to the Marikina-San Mateo boundary. This does not join accessions to the paper's five stations; retain the station and near-boundary assignment as unresolved. See national/reviews/ncr-marikina-2011-coarse-municipal-boundary-crosscheck-20261119.json.

Figure 1 names five numbered Marikina-system stations in north-to-south order, which is spatially consistent with the five GenBank coordinate clusters, but supplies no cluster/accession-to-station table. Treat this only as a candidate sequence correspondence; all individual station links remain unverified. See national/reviews/ncr-marikina-2011-figure1-coordinate-cluster-sequence-review-20261119.json.

The official UPLB repository catalogs Glorina D. Perez-Orozco's 2008 estero thesis as an MS Environmental Science thesis, but its full text is unavailable. This conflicts with the DLSU 2008 abstract's PhD wording and does not resolve overlap with the 2012 chapter or station-level fish data. See national/reviews/ncr-orozco-2008-thesis-catalog-access-review-20261119.json.

The 2023 Elsevier fish-microplastics paper is listed as published by PubMed and Ateneo, but a duplicate Ateneo Archium record says withdrawn. Publisher highlights mention Marikina janitor fish, while the accessible abstract does not allocate its scientific-name list by river and the common-name crosswalk is unresolved. Keep it research-only; add no species, occurrence, food-safety, or water-safety rows.

The 2019 Paco/Vitas tilapia biomonitoring paper used juvenile Nile tilapia procured from Cartimar pet market and exposed them in aquaria to water collected from the esteros; the fish are laboratory subjects, not estero captures. A closely matching 2018 DLSU thesis catalog record is unavailable in full text and is not counted as a separate survey. Add no NCR tilapia occurrence or species row from these records; see national/reviews/ncr-paco-vitas-2019-tilapia-biomonitoring-occurrence-exclusion-review-20261119.json.

The EMB-hosted Manila North WRF EPRMP documents three Estero de Vitas freshwater stations, plankton sampling, and macroinvertebrate sampling. The reviewed ecology chapter contains no fish method or taxa; that is a source-coverage limit, not evidence of fish absence. It adds waterbody context only; see national/reviews/ncr-vitas-manila-north-wrf-eprmp-freshwater-fish-scope-review-20261119.json.

The NFRDI 2014–2015 experimental otter-trawl survey reports a historical top-50 fish-and-invertebrate table grouped by broad Manila Bay sectors including Cavite and Metro Manila. It has no digital haul-coordinate table; the table was not transcribed, and the sectors are not municipality or legal-water boundaries. Keep this shared marine evidence research-only; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2017-manila-bay-trawl-sector-catch-scope-review-20261119.json.

The 2018 NAST Manila Bay fish-landing abstract reports 218 fish-and-invertebrate taxa from 16 landing sites (2012–2015), but gives no site-by-site table or capture-origin records. Its dates and three shared authors overlap the NFRDI 2014–2015 experimental-trawl paper, but the sampling frames differ and a data/program lineage is unconfirmed. Do not add the totals or infer sector-level presence; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2018-nast-manila-bay-landing-trawl-lineage-review-20261119.json.

The NFRDI 2012–2015 ichthyoplankton paper reports 3,008 fish larvae across 34 families; the separate NAST abstract reports 860 larvae across 28 families for 2017. Both describe eight stations and share three authors, but station spacing differs and no coordinate-linked species dataset was found. Keep the windows separate and family-level evidence research-only; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2017-manila-bay-ichthyoplankton-source-screen-20261119.json.

The DPWH Phase IV Supplemental EIS reports one 5 September 2014 gillnet sampling event at Marikina Bridge and names Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus as its only fish observed. Eschmeyer’s Catalog of Fishes currently treats that exact name as valid, which is a nomenclatural match only and does not verify the survey specimen. Keep it separate from the Phase II aggregate counts, the December 2013 Phase III passage, older secondary fish lists, and the distinct 2021 PAREX survey. No count, voucher-linked identity, current-presence, legal, or safety claim is established; EIS reuse terms remain unresolved. See national/reviews/ncr-marikina-pmrcip-phase-iv-fish-survey-review-20261120.json and national/reviews/ncr-marikina-pterygoplichthys-disjunctivus-name-crosscheck-20261120.json.

DENR-NCR Annual Report 2025 Section C lists 52 Pasig River system management entries in four clusters (15/15/10/12); the list remains a management scope, not a validated complete waterbody inventory. Cluster III’s ten labels have independent official name/locality text for eight exact waterway names and one orthographic candidate (Ermitanyo/Ermitaño); “Guadalupe Nuevo” remains unresolved because official Makati sources use it as a barangay and monitoring-station label. Estero de Sta. Clara / Sta. Clara Creek remains a possible name relationship, not a confirmed feature merge. No geometry, fish rows, or app records were added; see national/reviews/ncr-prcmo-2025-pasig-system-52-entry-scope-review-20261120.json and national/reviews/ncr-prcmo-cluster-iii-independent-name-crosswalk-20261120.json.

The 20 November Cluster IV crosswalk found six labels with exact independent waterway-name support, three variant/relationship candidates, one name whose River classification remains unresolved, and two area labels. The report separately uses Cluster IV for Manila Baseco/Parola cleanup context and for the Pateros/Taguig/Marikina/Pasig management list; leave this inconsistency unresolved and keep Baseco/Parola as Manila area contexts. No geometry, species, or app records were added. See national/reviews/ncr-prcmo-cluster-iv-independent-name-crosswalk-20261120.json.

The 20 November Cluster I crosswalk found exact independent name support for 14 of 15 labels; Estero de Uli-uli remains a name-form candidate. The 2020 LRT EIS states a 29-estero aggregate but the reviewed named list contains 20, so it is not used as a complete inventory. No geometry, fish evidence, or public records were added. See national/reviews/ncr-prcmo-cluster-i-independent-name-crosswalk-20261120.json.

The Cluster II independent name crosswalk found exact name support for 14 of 15 labels and one accent-only form candidate for Estero de Santibañez. Tanque/Tangue, Balete/Beata, Tripa de Galina/Gallina, Culiat/Culliat, and San Francisco River/Estero de San Francisco remain source distinctions; the 2020 EIS has inconsistent lists and a 29-versus-20 count gap. No feature links, geometry, fish assertions, or public-app records were added. See national/reviews/ncr-prcmo-cluster-ii-independent-name-crosswalk-20261120.json.

The Annual Report's separate Table 10 lists 17 River/Estero labels and 1,248 inventoried establishments. Twelve labels exactly match names in the 52-entry management set; five remain spelling, order, punctuation, or class-suffix candidates. The report does not explain whether its separate 152-establishment Pasig River survey and 1,248 Table 10 total share a sampling frame. These operational counts are not waterbody totals or fish evidence; no merges, geometries, species rows, or app records were added. See national/reviews/ncr-prcmo-establishment-table-waterway-scope-crosswalk-20261120.json.

SCSSAP Chapter 4 provides historical fish-table leads for LPPWP and TMTP: 20 and 52 listed entries, while the chapter reports 56 fish species combined. Its underlying Ancog et al. report is cited as undated; methods, survey dates, site-level roster reconciliation, specimen basis, and redistribution terms remain unresolved. No species, occurrence, waterbody feature, geometry, or app rows were added. See national/reviews/ncr-scssap-lppwp-tmtp-fish-list-scope-review-20261120.json.

GBIF CoL XR matched 34 of 35 distinct binomial strings as exact accepted-name candidates and one as an exact synonym; three source-row family strings differ from the matcher. The separate rank screen has since covered the 29 non-binomial rows with genus/order-only queries: 16 exact genus-name matches, one order match, and three weak or higher-rank candidates. These do not identify species or fish in either park; preserve all source labels, numbered placeholders, and site rows. See national/reviews/ncr-scssap-lppwp-tmtp-taxonomy-crosswalk-20261120.json and national/reviews/ncr-scssap-lppwp-tmtp-unresolved-fish-genera-20261120.json.

A bounded Eschmeyer Catalog of Fishes search screen now covers all 35 CoL XR binomials: 28 query names have a current “Valid as” status matching the query, while two source labels have current-name discrepancies. The Catalog treats the historical Ambassis gymnocephalus combination as a synonym of Ambassis ambassis and lists the historical Crenimugil seheli usage under Moolgarda seheli; keep both source labels unchanged pending study-level identity review. The other 28 status matches are nomenclatural context only, not specimen identification. No species, occurrence, geometry, or app rows were added. See national/reviews/ncr-scssap-lppwp-tmtp-remaining-col-fish-names-20261120.json.

The 29 residual SCSSAP labels remain unresolved below genus/order level. A specialist Catalog genus check found exact records for Platycephalus and comparison forms Sardinella, Leiognathus, Amblygobius, and Hyporhamphus, but no exact records for the printed forms Sardinela, Leignathus, Ambyglobius, and Hyporhampus. These are name-level leads only: no source spellings were corrected, numbered rows merged, or species/app data added. See national/reviews/ncr-scssap-lppwp-tmtp-unresolved-fish-genera-20261120.json and national/reviews/ncr-scssap-lppwp-tmtp-fish-catalog-genera-crosscheck-20261120.json.

The official 2013 LPPCHEA Ramsar Information Sheet reports eight fish from a 2001 ERDB survey; JICA repeats the same list and explicitly cites that RIS, so it is not independent corroboration. A 2023 Bacoor committee report states an unattributed aggregate count of eight without naming taxa or a source. The primary ERDB report remains unlocated; the RIS bibliography lead Alba et al. (2009) is not linked specifically to the fish paragraph. Keep all material research-only and seek the primary report before any taxon/site assertion. See national/reviews/ncr-lppchea-ramsar-2013-erdb-fish-lineage-review-20261120.json.

A third-party indexed copy of DENR (2012), Saving the Last Coastal Frontier, reports eight juvenile-to-sub-adult fish at LPPCHEA but does not cite the survey in the fish paragraph; indexed name strings may contain OCR errors. A later JICA report also reports eight juvenile fish and cites the Framework Plan nearby, but the citation scope for that sentence is unclear. These are overlapping secondary leads, not independent confirmations. The official plan copy and primary ERDB survey remain unlocated. See national/reviews/ncr-lppchea-denr-2012-framework-plan-fish-lineage-followup-20261120.json.

Su et al. (2009) is a separately dated primary heavy-metal sampling paper for fish caught by bottom trawl in the Las Piñas–Parañaque Lagoon in Sep–Nov 2007. Table 2 gives ten fish labels, but no counts per taxon, fish-specific coordinates, vouchers, exact LPPCHEA-boundary crosswalk, or item-specific reuse license. Two source spelling differences remain unresolved. Do not publish or merge it with the 2001 ERDB/Ramsar sample; see national/reviews/ncr-lpp-lagoon-su-et-al-2009-fish-sample-review-20261120.json.

Su et al. (2013) reports a Manila Bay coastal-lagoon trawl sample of five taxa, all already listed by Su et al. (2009), using the same north-to-south-and-back route and FishBase identification. It cites the 2009 paper but gives no collection date or explicit specimen-pool link; count it as overlapping research lineage, not an independent survey or new taxon evidence. Its locality does not name LPPCHEA, and the article states all rights reserved. See national/reviews/ncr-manila-bay-su-et-al-2013-lead-fish-lineage-review-20261120.json.

An official Eschmeyer Catalog cross-check found six Table 2 binomials with current-name matches, two current-name comparison candidates (Liza subviridis / Planiliza subviridis; Mugil melinopterus / Chelon melinopterus), and one unresolved Stolephorus source label. The Catalog lists commersonii as a spelling used for Stolephorus commersonnii, but it does not identify the lagoon specimen; the table form comersonii remains distinct. No source identity or app occurrence was promoted. See national/reviews/ncr-lpp-lagoon-su-et-al-2009-catalog-name-crosswalk-review-20261120.json.

Two separate Albatross-era Smithsonian paratype lots (USNM 138518 and 138534) and the 2025 Philippine fish type checklist were cross-checked; neither voucher is linked to Su et al. (2009), so the 2007 Stolephorus identity remains unresolved. Keep this lineage research-only; see national/reviews/ncr-lpp-stolephorus-historical-voucher-lineage-review-20261120.json.

A SESAM Library PDF compiled as of January 2024 includes an abstract entry for Perez-Orozco’s 2008 thesis and the same four aggregated fish labels from San Miguel and Quiapo Estero. It is not the thesis and adds no station-level or independent survey evidence. Preserve the MS/PhD discrepancy and 2008/2012 lineage hold; see national/reviews/ncr-orozco-2008-uplb-abstract-access-refresh-20261120.json.

The 1996 DLSU repository abstract for Estero Aviles describes water-quality sampling at Fifth St., Pumping Station, Buencamino St., and Matienza St.; it provides no fish taxa or fish-specific station results, and the article upload is unavailable. Keep the fish evidence unresolved and do not treat the missing abstract details as absence. See national/reviews/ncr-estero-aviles-1996-fish-study-access-review-20261120.json.

ERDB FY2022 Q2/Q3 reports list the Tanza Marine Tree Park ecological characterization as a proposal under review; the aggregate Q2 hold remark is not project-specific and Q3 blank output cells are not zero evidence. No completed fish survey or fish dataset is established. Seek a later final report/status record; see national/reviews/ncr-tmtp-erdb-2022-proposal-status-review-20261120.json.

A separate Catalog/FAO taxonomy screen for EIS Table 2-35 found two family-field discrepancies (Anodontostoma chacunda: EIS Clupeidae versus Catalog Dorosomatidae; Arius manillensis: EIS Plotosidae versus Catalog/FAO Ariidae) and a Mugil cephalus species-complex caveat. Preserve source strings and taxonomy crosswalk separately; no specimen identities or occurrences were added. See national/reviews/ncr-navotas-eis-table-2-35-taxonomy-crosscheck-20261120.json.

The EIS shorthand “Navotas CLUP, 2011” likely refers to a separately listed City Ecological Profile 2011; the exact original fishery pages remain inaccessible. The official 2016–2025 CLUP repeats four vernacular names but supplies no Latin-name validation or occurrence details. Keep all four leads research-only; see national/reviews/ncr-navotas-2011-ecological-profile-citation-reconciliation-20261120.json.

The 2024 Navotas-Malabon-Tullahan article's introduction gives six local-name/scientific-name pairs, but its cited CLUP Part 4 does not contain the crosswalk; CLUP Part 3 lists names only. All six remain unverified for Navotas and research-only, with no species or occurrence rows admitted. See national/reviews/ncr-navotas-nmt-intro-name-crosswalk-review-20261120.json.

A 2023 BFAR NCR retail price report associates Asohos with Sillago spp. in a row whose summary source area is Navotas; Sapsap with Leiognathus spp.; Salinas with Sardinella lemuru; and Tunsoy with several Sardinella rows. Market labels/source areas are aggregated and not specimen or capture evidence. No species or occurrence data were admitted. See national/reviews/ncr-navotas-bfar-2023-market-name-crosswalk-review-20261120.json.

regions.name: Region III (Central Luzon)
openWork: The BMB 2014 Atlas count crosswalk matches the RDP's 168 breakdown at category/count level (153 river systems; 11 lakes, three reservoirs and one swamp), but source lineage, the RDP's separate 202-river statement, all 153 named river systems, current identity and geometry remain unresolved; do not treat this as a verified inventory.

The 70-query CoL XR screen returned one Angat River locality row and 69 bounded zeroes. Follow-up linked it to BPC001-13/ANAd1, source-reported as Arius dispar, while the GBIF Backbone maps the BIN to Netuma thalassina; the BOLD BIN export does not resolve that specimen. A local FAO/HydroRIVERS screen places the source coordinate 0.7 km from an unnamed modeled reach; it is inside a simplified 2020 Bulacan polygon and shares the modeled MAIN_RIV grouping nearest to the GeoNames Angat River point. This supports plausibility only: the GeoNames point is not a route, the reach is unnamed, the exact reach and coordinate uncertainty remain unresolved, and the source chains are not independent. Keep the candidate research-only. The 69 zeroes do not establish absence.

The Pantabangan 2026 journal abstract reports 40 COI sequences/nine species, numerically matching the 2013 GenBank submission's 40 records/nine submitted names; the exact sequence set is unverified. Four earlier Micropterus and two Coptodon GenBank records have Pantabangan locality metadata from 2012, while the abstract calls those two taxa first records. The publisher full text is access-gated and no accession table was found in the bounded search, so retain this as an unresolved crosswalk/first-record conflict. Do not merge the 2013 records, 2026 article, or 2024–2025 student manuscript. See national/reviews/central-luzon-pantabangan-2026-article-access-followup-20261119.json.
Complete separate evidence and coverage results for Pampanga River reaches, Angat and Pantabangan reservoirs, Candaba wetland, tributaries, coast and estuaries.

Publisher-indexed full Silliman Journal text is now queryable and the methods, Nueva Ecija Tables 1-3, and Paitan discussion were re-reviewed. It supports two historical Paitan candidates: Leiopotherapon plumbeus (explicitly named in discussion) and Oreochromis niloticus (a non-empty Paitan Lake cell in Table 3); no additional fish is assigned from flattened rows. Both names are valid in the 2026 Catalog of Fishes, but this does not re-identify specimens or establish current presence. Field dates, vouchers, and rights remain unresolved. The separate janitor-fish lead is repeated through related secondary reports with a Pterygoplichthys parotalis / P. pardalis spelling conflict. The original Agasen report was not obtained; NISSAP is genus-level, and the 2009 report does not resolve presence or absence. Chavez et al. (2006) sampled five Laguna de Bay-basin sites but not Paitan. Do not create species assertions or absence claims. Vaca remains a separate unresolved reservoir: the 2021 joint stocking counts are unallocated, and PIDS provides historical downstream water-quality context but no fish inventory. See national/reviews/central-luzon-paitan-silliman-indexed-text-refresh-20261119.json, national/reviews/central-luzon-vaca-water-quality-and-fish-source-gap-20261119.json, national/reviews/central-luzon-paitan-historical-fish-name-crosscheck-20261119.json, and national/reviews/central-luzon-paitan-janitor-fish-source-conflict-followup-20261119.json.

The refreshed 2020 Candaba source reports one representative specimen per species group deposited at PSAU, but no accession numbers, field dates, site matrix, or item-specific reuse license; keep it research-only pending independent checks.

The UPLB-provided 1988 Habito thesis abstract reports eight freshwater fish species in eight families from a June–October 1987 survey but provides no fish species names. The official UPLB record says the document is unavailable online and identifies a physical UPLB Main Library Special Collections holding, call number LG 995 1988 Z62 H33. Current access and reproduction rules are unknown; no taxa or maps were extracted. See national/reviews/central-luzon-candaba-habito-1988-thesis-access-review-20261119.json.

Garcia (2010) publisher abstract reports 21 fish species caught in Candaba wetland during 2007–2008 and length-weight relationships for 18 species across 14 families, but no individual names. Direct Wiley full-text retrieval returned 403/timeouts and the bounded exact-title/DOI search found no clearly author-hosted copy. Treat this as an aggregate historical lead; no taxa or app rows were added. See national/reviews/central-luzon-candaba-garcia-2010-fulltext-access-review-20261119.json.

The 2020 publisher paper cites a Bautista & Barila Candaba fish-inventory thesis as 2013 in the introduction and 2003 in the bibliography; the cited title also prints 'Swamo'. A bounded exact-title/author and PSAU/Pampanga Agricultural College search found no independent catalog record or copy. This does not establish that none exists. Keep it as a year-conflicted bibliographic lead only; no thesis species data, app rows, or reuse rights were verified. See national/reviews/central-luzon-candaba-bautista-barila-citation-review-20261119.json.

Santos et al. (2010) reports 844 Leiopotherapon plumbeus specimens aggregated across seven localities. Its ResearchGate author-uploaded text describes Maasin River as a Pampanga tributary in Barangay San Agustin, Candaba, and calls the population native; a Maasin-specific sample count, date, voucher, or item reuse license remains unverified. ResearchGate warns the upload may be copyrighted. Keep as a historical research lead; see national/reviews/central-luzon-candaba-2010-maasin-silver-perch-review-20261119.json and national/reviews/central-luzon-candaba-2010-maasin-rg-fulltext-followup-20261119.json.

The 2019 Bagac conference paper is now identified and its 17/5 totals match the goby synthesis. Keep it separate from the 2022 15-taxon survey and later three-river surveys until field dates, possible sample overlap, and reuse are resolved.

The 2024 Angat ASH abstract names five fish and broad gut-content categories, but has no dated fish-to-site matrix, voucher crosswalk, quantitative prey rows, or item-specific reuse license; retain as research-only and seek an author-hosted full paper or data supplement.

The 19 November National Museum crosswalk shows that the 524-row OBIS refresh mirrors the same GBIF occurrence records; do not count it as an independent L3 species batch. It does not resolve capture waters or other shared-bay sources. Keep Manila Bay shared with L1/L2 and Bataan, Zambales, and Aurora coastal scopes distinct; see national/reviews/manila-bay-national-museum-gbif-obis-crosswalk-20261119.json.

The NFRDI 2014–2015 experimental otter-trawl survey reports a historical top-50 fish-and-invertebrate table grouped by broad Manila Bay sectors including Cavite and Metro Manila. It has no digital haul-coordinate table; the table was not transcribed, and the sectors are not municipality or legal-water boundaries. Keep this shared marine evidence research-only; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2017-manila-bay-trawl-sector-catch-scope-review-20261119.json.

The 2018 NAST Manila Bay fish-landing abstract reports 218 fish-and-invertebrate taxa from 16 landing sites (2012–2015), but gives no site-by-site table or capture-origin records. Its dates and three shared authors overlap the NFRDI 2014–2015 experimental-trawl paper, but the sampling frames differ and a data/program lineage is unconfirmed. Do not add the totals or infer sector-level presence; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2018-nast-manila-bay-landing-trawl-lineage-review-20261119.json.

The NFRDI 2012–2015 ichthyoplankton paper reports 3,008 fish larvae across 34 families; the separate NAST abstract reports 860 larvae across 28 families for 2017. Both describe eight stations and share three authors, but station spacing differs and no coordinate-linked species dataset was found. Keep the windows separate and family-level evidence research-only; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2017-manila-bay-ichthyoplankton-source-screen-20261119.json.

The 2009 Silliman reference list cites the 2005 CLSU Environmental Management Institute volume Biodiversity and two Nueva Ecija freshwater-fish chapters. CLSU's official library site links its OPAC, but the catalog query was unavailable and no lawful full-text copy was retrieved. The citation trail does not resolve field dates, site assignments, vouchers, data independence, or reuse rights. Keep the 2005 lead research-only; no species rows or absence claims added. See national/reviews/central-luzon-clsu-emi-biodiversity-2005-access-review-20261120.json.

A follow-up attempt on 20 November used the current official Silliman OJS article page, but its PDF route returned 404; the former publisher download route returned 502. The browser-readable article text remains available through indexing, but no page image was obtained to verify the table cells visually. Keep the unresolved species-to-waterbody cells held; do not map flattened rows. See national/reviews/central-luzon-silliman-2009-table-visual-access-followup-20261120.json.

The 2018 SNMC EPRMP reports a 2006 six-site fish list but its prose names seven fish while the indexed table lists ten; cells, spellings, evidence modes, currentness and reuse remain unresolved. The 2022 Eagle and 2023 SNMC EPRMPs repeat the same May 2022 four-station Conlong/Salapangan assessment and fish observation statements; count them as overlapping source material, not independent confirmation. Poecilia reticulata at W02-W04 was seen but not sampled; one W03 tilapia is unidentified, while bulig/hito are interview leads. Keep the evidence research-only; see national/reviews/central-luzon-bulacan-snmc-eprmp-freshwater-fish-review-20261120.json and national/reviews/central-luzon-bulacan-eagle-snmc-conlong-salapangan-campaign-lineage-review-20261120.json.

The 2020 Eagle Cement EIS names six fish/other-fauna labels from a combined resident-interview/literature method but assigns none to the four freshwater stations. A 2022 Samar EIS repeats near-identical method wording and most labels with a different count, creating a template/lineage warning rather than corroboration. Keep all labels research-only and unassigned; see national/reviews/central-luzon-bulacan-eagle-cement-eis-fish-context-review-20261120.json.

regions.name: Region I (Ilocos Region)
openWork: Build the region's waterbody manifest across Lower Agno, Abra, tributaries, Lingayen Gulf, coast and estuaries.

Keep Dantis and Lacap's five-station 2018 Agno macrofauna research-only. CoL XR has 21 exact accepted-name matches, one variant and one synonym match; a separate Catalog review covers five selected labels, while three genus-level rows and a Moolgarda pedaraki authority conflict remain unresolved. ARB5 municipality/reach, ARB4 place-name, and month/season conflicts are still open; the pooled table is not a species-by-station matrix. The separate goby synthesis row remains a bibliography lead only. See national-agno-pangasinan-macrofauna-review-20261030.json, national-agno-pangasinan-taxonomy-crosscheck-20261030.json, national-agno-station-locality-crosswalk-20261030.json, national-agno-date-locality-clarification-search-20261030.json, and national-agno-taxonomic-authority-crosscheck-20261030.json.

The Bayaoas River BSRIP 2019/2020 EIS drafts describe one historical five-station freshwater survey, but their fish narrative conflicts with the table and reuse terms are unverified; keep it research-only and do not double-count the draft versions. A bounded Catalog crosscheck gives candidates for the two misspelled binomials only; retain Glossogobius sp. and Oreochromis sp. at genus level. See national/reviews/region01-bayaoas-river-bsrip-eis-fish-source-screen-20261119.json and national/reviews/region01-bayaoas-river-fish-label-crosscheck-20261120.json.

The 2023 Binday Dam paper reports two fish-study locations (Colisao upstream and Aramal downstream) but not numeric fish counts; the abstract/table spelling differs, and its native/invasive claim conflicts. A bounded Catalog crosscheck records candidates for seven name groups while retaining two genus/family-level labels; it does not validate specimens. The publisher page lists both CC BY-NC 4.0 and CC BY 4.0, so keep the evidence research-only. See national/reviews/region01-binday-dam-soriano-fish-source-review-20261119.json and national/reviews/region01-binday-dam-fish-name-crosscheck-20261120.json.

Rojas (2023) reports a three-station Govantes River FAD assessment in Vigan, with 20 claimed macrofauna taxa but 19 Figure 1 caption labels; table cells, exact sampling dates, voucher links and extracted-data reuse terms remain unresolved. A bounded Catalog/WoRMS crosscheck records candidates for 13 body-listed fish labels, but does not verify specimens or resolve the count mismatch. Keep the evidence research-only; see national/reviews/region01-govantes-river-rojas-macrofauna-source-screen-20261119.json and national/reviews/region01-govantes-river-fish-name-crosscheck-20261120.json.

Gaerlan et al. (2018) summarize 2009–2013 small-pelagic fishery landings from ten Lingayen Gulf landing sites and list 20 dominant source labels, but publish no species-by-landing/capture-site matrix; current journal license pages conflict for this 2018 paper. Keep it research-only; see national/reviews/region01-lingayen-small-pelagic-gaerlan-2009-2013-source-review-20261119.json.

The MMSU catalog abstract for Mapalo and Rigua's 2021 Oaig-Upay-Abulao River thesis reports 14 taxa and names three fish, but the 66-leaf thesis is marked Room Use Only and no full checklist, station crosswalk or reuse terms are available. Keep this as an access-limited research lead; see national/reviews/region01-oaig-upay-abulao-mmsu-thesis-catalog-access-review-20261119.json.

For Paoay Lake, Aquino et al. (2008) provide a zooplankton survey and only PAMB-personal-communication fish labels, while Magistrado et al. (2026) provide non-indigenous-species risk categories rather than a new fish survey. Keep both as research-only leads; see national/reviews/region01-paoay-lake-fish-evidence-screen-20261119.json.

The 2026 Maluyo River article reports 16 fauna rows, but its methods do not identify actual fish sampling effort, dates, station assignments or vouchers; its fish labels include mixed taxonomic resolution and the publisher page has conflicting license statements. Keep research-only; see national/reviews/region01-maluyo-river-fauna-source-screen-20261119.json.

The DMMMSU repository exposes only an abstract for a 2021 transplanted-mangrove fish study in La Union. It reports aggregate counts at three unnamed stations and the unresolved spelling Salotherodon melanotheron; no full fish list, method or license was verified. Keep this as an abstract-only lead; see national/reviews/region01-la-union-transplanted-mangrove-thesis-abstract-screen-20261119.json.

The PSA Region I 2024 Municipal Fisheries Situationer reports provincial marine and inland production and top common/local catch labels, including Mullet (Kapak) and Freshwater Goby (Biya). It names no waterbody or source site and gives no scientific names or vouchers; production is not occurrence or abundance evidence. Use only to prioritize distinct inland and marine source searches; see national/reviews/region01-la-union-psa-municipal-fisheries-2024-source-screen-20261119.json.

Balneg et al. (2025) provide a dated Caba bottom-set-gillnet catch study across four barangays/eight fishing spots. Its 43 table labels include a crab and Mugil sp.; the catch tables are site-aggregated, voucher IDs are absent, several names/statistics conflict internally, effort wording is unresolved, and no article license was verified. A separate authoritative catalog crosscheck suggests name-string variants but does not identify sampled specimens; keep research-only pending taxon, voucher, effort, site-crosswalk and rights checks. See national/reviews/region01-caba-bottom-set-gillnet-catch-composition-review-20261119.json and national/reviews/region01-caba-gillnet-taxon-spelling-crosscheck-20261119.json.

Allayban et al. (2026) report an undated reef-fish visual census at Calay-Ab and the proposed Calay-Ab-Sived MPA, with 43 source-listed fish-name rows and 1,562 total counts. A bounded catalog review provides candidate spellings for four table-variant groups but confirms no sampled organism. GPS/map text supplies no reusable coordinates or geometry. Keep it research-only, do not treat the proposed MPA as a legal boundary, and do not infer present fishing rules or access. See national/reviews/region01-sto-domingo-calay-ab-reef-fish-source-review-20261119.json and national/reviews/region01-sto-domingo-reef-fish-name-crosscheck-20261119.json.

The 2025 SSRN Viray Watershed item is currently an abstract-only Pangasinan freshwater lead. Its indexed abstract names six fish but exposes no fish-event dates, methods, constituent waterbody/station crosswalk, vouchers, coordinates, or reuse license; the page and linked PDF returned 403 during review. Keep the labels research-only and continue seeking accessible full text or independent, site-resolved Pangasinan river evidence; see national/reviews/region01-viray-watershed-fish-source-screen-20261119.json.

Peralta-Milan and Salmo's 2013 Lingayen Gulf mangrove-fish article has conflicting repository status: UPLB record 4086 explicitly marks it withdrawn, while duplicate UPLB/Ateneo records expose only an abstract. Hold its reported 50-species total and site claims from evidence until an authoritative correction/replacement or withdrawal explanation is located; see national/reviews/region01-lingayen-mangrove-fish-withdrawal-screen-20261119.json.

Paz-Alberto and Teñoso's 2013 Silliman Journal study reports a November–December 2009 snorkeling visual census in the Arnedo, Balingasay, Binabalian, and Victory MPAs of Bolinao, with 20 fish taxa claimed. Taxon spellings conflict across abstract and tables; a separate WoRMS/Catalog of Fishes check records candidate spellings but confirms no sampled organism. No machine-readable station coordinates or vouchers were found, and no item-specific article-data reuse license was verified. Keep research-only; do not project the historical MPA/no-take description as current rules or infer present occurrence, access, safety, or catchability. See national/reviews/region01-bolinao-four-mpa-fish-survey-source-review-20261119.json and national/reviews/region01-bolinao-fish-name-variant-crosscheck-20261119.json.

Paz-Alberto and Teñoso's 2011 Silliman Journal study reports four fish and 14 invertebrate taxa from late-2009 mangrove sampling in the same four Bolinao barangays, using gill nets and cover pots. It lacks machine-readable sampling coordinates and reviewed voucher identifiers; its derived-data reuse permission is unverified. The three high-importance abstract labels are invertebrates in the results, and the prose/table spelling of Periopthalmus differs. Keep this mangrove evidence separate from the same authors' 2013 MPA visual census and research-only; see national/reviews/region01-bolinao-mangrove-fish-invertebrate-source-review-20261119.json.

A bounded WoRMS/Catalog of Fishes/FishBase check maps the four 2011 Bolinao table-label groups to candidate accepted names, including Liza argentea to Gracilimugil argenteus and the Periopthalmus spelling variants to a Periophthalmus barbarus candidate. It confirms no study specimen; preserve source labels and keep taxon candidates research-only. See national/reviews/region01-bolinao-mangrove-fish-name-crosscheck-20261119.json.

NFRDI/SEAFDEC's 2022 Bolinao fisheries landing report covers 2018-2020, claims 176 species types in aggregate, and names seven fish taxa in selected municipality/ground catch summaries. It does not expose a complete 176-name checklist, individual catch events, coordinates, or a Bolinao-municipal-waters species breakdown. Its printed reuse permission is limited to educational/non-profit purposes with attribution; commercial use needs prior written permission. Keep the claims research-only and preserve the West Philippine Sea, coastal-water, Caquiputan Channel, and municipal-water labels separately; see national/reviews/region01-bolinao-seafdec-landing-survey-source-review-20261119.json.

The related NFRDI/SEAFDEC April-June 2018 report lists landing centers and quarterly catch/length-frequency aggregates for Coron, Masinloc, and Bolinao, but its published tables contain no fish-name rows. Its stated collection method mentions species identification by gear, but the species-resolved data are not included; keep this as fishery-method/source context only. The Bolinao quarter may overlap the later 2018-2020 report, so do not sum totals. See national/reviews/region01-bolinao-seafdec-q2-2018-landing-data-source-screen-20261119.json.

Cerezo et al. (2018) report 15 fish-name labels from Buenlag-Sabangan River, Binmaley, but field dates, named fish stations, vouchers, source-by-name provenance, and item-specific reuse terms are unresolved. Keep research-only; see national/reviews/region01-binmaley-buenlag-sabangan-macrofauna-source-screen-20261119.json.

The PSSN 2014 conference abstracts report aggregate aquatic-fauna totals and a few name strings for Dagupan City rivers and Buenlag-Sabangan River, but no complete lists, dates, named fish stations, methods or coordinates. Do not merge the Buenlag abstract with Cerezo et al. (2018); survey lineage and reuse terms are unresolved. The ATI research roster is only a lead to the full Dagupan study. Keep research-only; see national/reviews/region01-pssn-dagupan-buenlag-aquatic-fauna-abstract-screen-20261119.json.

De Guzman et al. (2020) visually report 38 fish-name rows and Sector I/III marks for modified-Danish-seine landings in Dec 2015–Jan 2016. Two vessels landed at Magsaysay Market; no haul coordinates, vouchers, or fish-to-site records are provided. The abstract/results say 22 families while the table/discussion show 21, and the article has no identified item-specific reuse license. Keep names as historical sector-scale research leads only; see national/reviews/region01-lingayen-danish-seine-catch-composition-review-20261119.json.

The official EMB-hosted Dumoloc SRIP EIS reports a 2019 electrofishing baseline at two Dumuloc River sites and seven source-name fish rows. A separate Catalog of Fishes/Philippine-checklist crosscheck records candidate names and preserves the Tukugobius generic-treatment and EIS spelling variants, but confirms no sampled specimens. Keep all rows research-only and do not map them; the original table layout, coordinates, vouchers, and reuse terms remain unresolved. See national/reviews/region01-dumuloc-river-eis-fish-source-review-20261119.json and national/reviews/region01-dumuloc-river-fish-name-crosscheck-20261120.json.

Keep the 2001 four-river edible-fauna paper held: its publisher PDF URL served unrelated gambling/SEO content in the 2026-11-20 follow-up, and bounded search found no trusted independent full text. Seek a publisher-confirmed, provenance-checked copy before resuming table/taxon review; continue independent dated river and coastal evidence meanwhile. See national/reviews/region01-abra-ilocos-2009-publisher-link-integrity-review-20261120.json.

Tenio et al. (2026) and its CC BY 4.0 dataset support historical station-level research extraction for Lower Agno ARB5 (10 table labels; 245 matrix individuals) and ARB6 (3 labels; 659 individuals). Article Table 4 station labels and dataset rows agree, but Wet/Dry-to-date mapping remains conflicting; ARB5 source locality San Roque, San Manuel conflicts with point screens returning San Nicolas, and ARB6's smaller reverse-geocoded locality differs from Viray. Keep the review research-only and do not project current species records or station points as river geometry; see national/reviews/region01-lower-agno-arb5-arb6-tenio-2026-station-fish-review-20261120.json and national-agno-station-locality-crosswalk-20261030.json.
Reconcile source-supported reach relationships with CAR without extending a reach-specific record across an entire basin.

A bounded 20-label WoRMS exact-name lookup found accepted records for all printed names; the Catalog also lists Decapterus tabl as valid. These matches do not identify Lingayen catch specimens, so retain the source strings verbatim and keep this historical gulf-level landing summary research-only; no site-level occurrences or public rows are admitted. See national/reviews/region01-lingayen-small-pelagic-gaerlan-fish-name-crosscheck-20261120.json.

The UP MSI 2024 State of the Coasts chapter summarizes a 2015 Cabugao reef assessment with 134 fish species across 33 families/subfamilies and aggregate station metrics, but no complete checklist, fish-by-station table, vouchers, or coordinates. Keep research-only and historical; seek the underlying NACRE-PEARRL records and reuse terms. See national/reviews/region01-cabugao-2015-reef-fish-assemblage-review-20261120.json.

JICA's 1997 Laoag River Basin Appendix K includes a secondary common/local-name fauna table referencing Paoay Lake National Park and Laoag River/offshore contexts. It has no scientific names or waterbody assignment per label, and the report date is not a field date. Keep as historical source-tracing context only; seek the underlying local-office records and do not create species occurrences. See national/reviews/region01-paoay-laoag-jica-1997-fauna-context-review-20261120.json.

Blanco (1956) documents a direct 1954–1955 goby-fry survey in Laoag River, listing 11 source fish names from brackish/fresh river portions and six postlarval run names, with qualitative stomach/feeding notes on juvenile gobies. The article also covers adjacent marine shores; preserve those contexts separately. Locality names have no station coordinates or taxon/date crosswalk, labels have no modern taxonomy/voucher check, and article reuse terms are unverified. Keep research-only and seek site-resolved, modern corroboration before public species or diet rows; see national/reviews/region01-laoag-river-blanco-1956-ipon-goby-fishery-review-20261120.json.

The Philippine eLib catalog gives an abstract for Ungson's 1984 Santa goby-fry thesis and explicitly marks the digital copy unavailable. The abstract says nine goby species were identified but names only Sicyopterus lacrymosus, Sicyoterus sp., and Chonophorus melanocephalus; it does not name the eight coastal barangays or assign labels to sites. FishBase independently lists a related 1985 Ungson–Hermes paper, but gives no full-text URL. Treat both as access leads, not a checklist or site-resolved occurrence evidence; see national/reviews/region01-santa-ilocos-sur-ungson-1984-thesis-and-1985-article-access-review-20261120.json.

The official MMSU and Quirino, Ilocos Sur notices establish a Northern Luzon goby-project lead and municipal coordination only; no sampling output, named waterbody, station, taxon or voucher is published. Keep this separate from Quirino Province in Region II and from the Cagayan/Ilocos Norte Nagao 2026 survey report. See national/reviews/region01-quirino-ilocos-sur-mmsu-northern-goby-project-context-review-20261120.json.

openWork: Continue the waterbody and fish-source sweep outside the Cagayan Riverine Zone, including Pacific-draining Isabela, Batanes islands, and separate Quirino and Nueva Vizcaya waters.

Treat Baleta and Baleta (2016) as a Palanan landing-list lead only: its 74-species claim has an unspecified survey year, no site-to-capture crosswalk, a suspect printed coordinate, and internal name/citation inconsistencies. Publisher PDF retrieval returned HTTP 403 on 2026-11-20; indexed text has noisy table alignment, so no name rows were transcribed. Obtain a readable publisher/author/library copy before page-image, taxonomy, and reuse review; see national/reviews/region02-palanan-2016-marine-seasonal-landings-review-20261120.json.

Review the EMB-indexed Ilaguen 3A Revised EIS freshwater fish list only as a source lead: Table 51 has ten rows including one genus-only name, conflicting spellings, no verified fish-site crosswalk, and a direct-PDF 403. Confirm the original table and survey methods before species extraction; see national/reviews/region02-isabela-ilaguen-3a-eis-freshwater-fish-list-access-review-20261120.json.

Encarnacion et al. (2017) is cross-checked through the abstract and methods: July 2014–June 2015 landing-center sampling in four Isabela coastal municipalities reports 23,980 fish, 238 species in aggregate, and three top catch shares, but no verified species-by-capture-site matrix. The species table remains unverified after page-render HTTP 429 and direct-download HTTP 403; conservation counts conflict and reuse terms are unresolved. See national/reviews/region02-isabela-waters-2014-2015-marine-landings-review-20261120.json.

The 2009–2013 Babuyan Channel assessment uses 12 named landing sites in six Cagayan municipalities; its stated 11-municipality fishing-ground extent is broader than that landing frame. Its 256-species/69-family aggregate has mixed-catch and internal count/category issues; the 2014–2015 Isabela study is a distinct, adjacent NSAP summary frame, but record or fishing-ground overlap is unresolved. Do not add either aggregate to a regional unique-species total. See national/reviews/region02-babuyan-isabela-nsap-landing-frame-crosscheck-20261120.json.

The NIA Magapuy–Paitan notices confirm separate May–June fish-trap sampling and an August flora/fauna inventory, but publish no fish list or site-resolved results. Seek the underlying report and keep the two field efforts distinct; see national/reviews/region02-magapuy-paitan-2025-flora-fauna-inventory-access-review-20261120.json.
Keep barcode field labels, market-purchase labels, coordinates, and drainage crosswalks held until specimen, date, site, and reuse checks resolve.
Reconcile coastal, estuarine, river, reservoir, lake, wetland, aquaculture, and infrastructure records as separate evidence contexts.

Hata et al. (2026) report three vouchered Decapterus smithvanizi specimens attributed by retailer interviews to capture off Santa Ana, Cagayan; specimens were purchased at Don Domingo Market in Tuguegarao on 29 January 2026. No coordinates or fishing-ground identity are published, and one lateral-line scale count conflicts with the identification text. Keep research-only under the article's CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 terms; see national/reviews/region02-cagayan-santa-ana-decapterus-smithvanizi-source-review-20261120.json.

The Guerrero (2022) Cagayan River paragraph claims eight freshwater fishes but names seven groups; its cited Lagasca (2013) news report lists eight regional freshwater taxa including snails, clams and prawns. The lineage and count remain unresolved, the ludong labels differ (Cestraeus plicatilis vs Cestraeus sp.), and neither source supports site-level rows. See national/reviews/region02-cagayan-river-2022-nast-2013-philstar-source-crosscheck-20261120.json.

Villarao et al. (2026) provide a single-taxon NSAP landings and stock assessment for common dolphinfish (Arayu) from 19 Batanes landing sites during 2014–2023. These are landing centers, not capture locations; no underlying catch extract or landing-to-ground crosswalk is published. Preserve the difference between the 2022–2023 troll-line-only FiSAT estimates and broader CMSY/SPR indicators; this does not establish a complete Batanes fish list or current stock advice. See national/reviews/region02-batanes-coryphaena-hippurus-stock-assessment-20261120.json.

Morales et al. (2016) report a historical Batanes NSAP assessment (2009–2013), naming 15 dominant marine catch taxa and an aggregate 580-species/66-family count. The full list was not extracted, the study period has an internal duration inconsistency, the Cheilopogon spilinopterus label and some stock metrics need review, and there is no taxon-to-capture-ground matrix or item-specific reuse license. Keep this research-only; see national/reviews/region02-batanes-morales-2016-municipal-marine-fishery-review-20261120.json.

The Batanes 2016 dolphinfish-prey statement traces to a 1982 NOAA/FAO synthesis of non-Philippine stomach samples: the nearly 25% flyingfish figure is from 373 adults off North Carolina, while a separate 46-fish Gulf Stream sample found no flyingfish. This is not local diet evidence or bait guidance; see national/reviews/region02-batanes-coryphaena-diet-source-crosscheck-20261120.json.

The Batanes 2016 catch label Cheilopogon spilinopterus is not yet taxonomically resolved. Eschmeyer's Catalog lists C. spilopterus and the separate C. spilonotopterus as valid, but the spelling match, duplicated common name with C. furcatus, and shared local name with C. nigricans do not identify a specimen; keep it research-only. See national/reviews/region02-batanes-cheilopogon-spilinopterus-taxonomy-crosscheck-20261120.json.

The official BMB TB 2017-05 annex points to generic reef-fish training/reference files and “Sample reef fish data”; the linked folder could not be inspected, and no source ties it to the Batanes CARE-CaDRES assessment. Keep the 2017 Batanes result aggregate-only; see national/reviews/region02-batanes-2017-bmb-research-materials-access-crosscheck-20261120.json.

Quimpo et al. (2019) provide a peer-reviewed upper-mesophotic fish list (80 of 138 comparison-list fish rows marked present) pooled across Luzon Strait/Batanes, Palawan, and KIG. The single presence column cannot assign detections to Batanes; keep all taxa research-only and seek a location-resolved matrix. See national/reviews/region02-batanes-quimpo-2019-luzon-strait-fish-supplement-crosscheck-20261120.json.
